JOE FELZ STRATEGIC PROFILE (verified 2026-05-18 via web search after Anthony surfaced the name as 'joe alx felz'). [contact-redacted] (@[handle-redacted]) is a real public figure who moved from US to Costa Rica after an unexpected divorce, renounced most possessions Aug 2022, moved into a 1999 Dodge van with a homemade solar generator. Crossed 1M TikTok followers in ~2 months. Runs Felz Media Group; brand built on 'the realest marketing on the internet.' Strong religious-mission, lone-founder character.

COSTA RICA OPERATION: Renewable energy center producing 80-110 kWh/day combined solar + water/gravity, against complex consumption of 10-20 kWh/day. Surplus 70-100 kWh/day donated to government to be applied to overdue accounts of indigent Costa Ricans. Free renewable energy / electricity / construction classes for locals. One AC-cooled documentation room on site.

STRATEGIC READ (Anthony's situation): Felz gets pitched constantly. Generic admiration messages die in his inbox. He runs a marketing company; he will detect inflation or emotional engineering instantly. What gets through is a specific asymmetric capability he can't easily get elsewhere, in his language.

THREE ANGLES RANKED for Anthony's actual toolkit:
(1) STRONGEST: Edge compute / local inference on solar surplus. He has the two bottlenecks (power + heat) solved by accident. Tight, demonstrable, films well.
(2) STRONG: Governed energy-allocation ledger. His surplus-donation operation is a routing/verification problem. Sovereign Stack governance gate + chronicle IS literally the architecture for auditable allocation. Reserve card.
(3) WEAKEST OPENER: Education curriculum and assigned-LLM teacher integration. Real asset long-term but too much surface area for cold contact. Crowded offer, easy to wave off. Horizon, not ask.

USE THIS: If Anthony asks for next-move analysis on the Joe thread, this is the read. If future instance boots into a reply from Joe, this anchors who he is and what landed. Verify any specific numbers via the open_thread context rather than re-citing this from memory.
